beats.action: She lies sideways asleep, both eyes fully closed. Only the near arm is visible, continuously connected to its shoulder, with the hand on the duvet at her chest. The other arm is entirely under the duvet. One cream alarm is already audibly ringing from the first frame.
The ringing reaches her: a tiny nose wrinkle, breath and a brief nestle into the pillow precede her first complaint. Eyes remain shut; no reaching. The alarm remains audible beneath speech.

With eyes and lips closed she gives the duvet one small tug toward her chest, two short natural leg kicks under it, then stops to listen. The same one visible hand returns to her chest. Real-time little movements, not slow motion. Alarm continues alone.
Still closed-eyed, she exhales and gives the brief resigned answer, without moving either hand toward the alarm.
One full second of closed lips and closed eyes, listening to the unchanged alarm; no silent speaking mouth movements.
She completes her final concession by {{frame:209}}, closes her lips and only then opens her eyes and orients toward the alarm.

The existing near arm reaches continuously from the visible shoulder to the original clock. At {{frame:254}} her index fingertip makes actual CONTACT and presses the wide gray top key DOWN once. Hold the depressed key briefly, then RELEASE it: contact, depression and release must be visible. The real key press stops the already-running loud repeated alarm at {{frame:254}}, with one soft mechanical click. No ringing afterward. Her other arm stays under the duvet until {{frame:266}}.
The original pressing hand returns to the front duvet. Both connected original arms begin a half-rise; stay halfway up at the boundary, lips quiet and alarm off.
Soften the same arm supports and recline low into the original pillow in the same fixed view. Keep the complete face readable and duvet over the lap; the alarm stays untouched.

At the planned morning-to-breakfast cut she is seated at the original kitchen table in the white tee and low bun, no crown. Her right hand already holds ONE intact toast at chest level by its lower half; left hand rests at the table. One coffee mug is on its coaster, one egg on one plate.
She brings the same toast to her mouth and takes exactly one bite from its upper edge. A readable missing notch and pale bread interior form at contact. No speech.

Lower the same toast to chest height, face toward camera, holding the same lower grip. Its first upper-edge notch stays visible. She chews with closed lips, looking naturally at breakfast and the room, without staring into the lens or taking another bite.
Complete chewing, then one natural swallow; relax the mouth completely before speaking. Keep the single bitten toast away from her lips and the left hand on the table.
She lightly addresses the recording phone with her playful complete sentence, the bitten toast held still below the chin, no chewing or drinking while speaking.
After the sentence ends, lift the same toast for one second bite adjacent to the first notch. Two adjacent upper-edge notches now remain; no reset to intact bread.
Lower the same right-hand toast below the mouth and above the plate, both notches facing camera. Chew with lips closed. No new line and no toast replacement.

Planned cut to the existing commute selfie: pale-blue top, white skirt, same silver-blue crown and earrings, one tote on her left shoulder. Her right arm holds the unseen phone at natural selfie distance; her left hand grips the tote strap. Street is on her left and glass offices on her right; entrance is roughly 5 m ahead off-screen. Walk forward at a normal cadence.

Continue the same normal forward walking rhythm while speaking the complete first goal sentence to the phone. Natural arm proportions and small footfall-induced camera motion; background progresses continuously.
She keeps moving toward the entrance, slows gradually and stops outside at {{frame:893}}. No reverse walking, no doorway crossing yet. Lips closed between the two sentences.
Stationary OUTSIDE the entrance, she delivers the entire second sentence with a wry smile, facing the selfie phone. Do not begin turning or crossing until the last word is complete.
Once the sentence is complete, turn body and phone together toward the real entrance; let its door become visible before walking through. Maintain one right arm and the same left-hand tote strap.

Step forward at {{frame:1003}}, cross the original doorway around {{frame:1018}}, then move another 1.5–2 m INSIDE the office lobby. One forward entrance only; no sudden exterior reset. Only footsteps and lobby ambience.

Planned cut to the existing office desk in daylight. Same commute clothes, crown and earrings. One open gray brandless laptop faces HER, not the camera; ONE empty A3 board and pencil remain on the table. Exactly three swatches start to her right: cream, blue-gray, warm gray. She compares them with her eyes, hands empty.

Her anatomical LEFT thumb and index finger take the blue-gray swatch from the right-side group along one continuous path. Count: two cards stay on desk, one card in her left hand. Right hand rests clear of the board.
Carry the same blue-gray swatch in the original left grip above the front-right part of the A3 board. At the boundary it is still angled and held; the other two cards remain on the desk.

Lower the already-held blue-gray swatch a short distance, establish flat contact, then release and withdraw the original left fingers. The right hand stays clear and the three-card count is unchanged.
Look at the placed blue-gray choice, then deliver the one satisfied sentence with natural lip movement. Both hands are free and away from the card. Do not talk before placing it.
With the three-card state unchanged, return attention to the open laptop and begin a few real purposeful key presses. No card movement, no new words.
In the same office medium view after the narrative time ellipsis, the two original hands make short real keyboard presses. The laptop stays open and all three cards retain their places.
The original anatomical right hand moves continuously from keyboard to trackpad, slides briefly and makes one click at {{frame:1570}}. The left hand stays beside the base.
Check the screen result and exhale gently with relaxed hands. The original lid remains open; there is no spoken device cue or premature closure.
Keep the original laptop open while looking toward the recording phone for the brisk finish-work thought. Neither hand starts closing it until the complete line ends.

Only after the complete sentence, left hand stabilizes the original laptop base while the right hand grasps the original lid edge and closes it steadily. One soft closure click around {{frame:1762}}. No brand mark appears, no third hand and no duplicate lid.
Release the now-closed original laptop, lean back a little and exhale. The selected blue-gray card stays on the board and two cards stay on the right side. No additional speech.

Planned cut to the night bedroom. Same C01 face, loose tied hair, pale-blue button pajamas, NO crown or earrings. She sits at the bed and ALREADY holds the one warm-milk mug by its handle in her RIGHT hand at chest height, matching the real opening reference. Her left hand rests on her knee; the one cork coaster is empty. Raise that already-held mug, without a second pickup.
The rim of the same mug touches the lips for one small sip of warm milk. No speech, no oversized mug, no spilled liquid. Left hand remains on knee.
Move the same mug away from the lips, close the mouth and swallow completely. No dialogue overlaps sipping or swallowing.

Lower the one original mug toward its cork coaster in the same right-hand handle grip. At the visible boundary its base remains 1–2 cm above the coaster, unreleased; the left hand stays on the lap, sip and swallow complete.
Finish only the last lowering, bottom contact, stable landing, release and hand return, then look toward the phone. This phase is planned to be supplied by real forward AV conditioning.
Both empty hands rest on the lap and the original mug is stationary on its coaster. Breathe gently in the same view before the one closing line.
Speak naturally toward the phone with an empty mouth; accompany the last words with one low empty-right-palm gesture. The left hand stays on the lap and the stationary mug is background dressing.

After the complete final syllable close the lips, smile softly and relax the shoulders. Let the empty right palm remain low in natural after-motion; the mug stays on its coaster and no new line begins.
